verdict: Con Edison grew revenue 8% to $4.9B on higher approved electric and gas rates and earned $766M, up 11% — a steady quarter for New York's main utility, with most of the revenue growth simply passing through the cost of energy it buys for customers.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was $4,913M, vs $4,530M a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Vs $1.90 a year ago; basic EPS was $2.07

kpis.label: Electric revenue
kpis.note: Up 9% — 89% of all revenue, driven by higher rate bases (the regulated value of its grid assets)

kpis.label: Net income
kpis.note: Up 11% from $688M a year ago; adjusted earnings were the same $766M

segments.name: Electric
segments.note: Delivering electricity in New York City and Westchester — by far the biggest business, growing as regulators approve higher rates to fund grid investment.

segments.name: Gas
segments.note: Delivering natural gas for heating and cooking.

segments.name: Steam
segments.note: The Manhattan steam system that heats many large buildings.

segments.name: Non-utility
segments.note: Small remaining non-utility activities — a rounding-sized line.

opex.name: Taxes, other than income taxes
opex.note: Mainly property taxes on the grid, pipes and plants — a huge, unavoidable cost for a utility, up 7% YoY.

opex.name: Other operations & maintenance
opex.note: Crews, repairs and running the electric, gas and steam networks day to day — down 2% YoY.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: A non-cash charge spreading the cost of poles, wires, pipes and plants over their long lives.

otherDetail: Other was -$149M, net: $168M of other income (including a $27M allowance for equity funds used during construction — a non-cash credit utilities are allowed to book while they build) minus $317M of net interest expense on the company's debt.
footerNote: Utility adaptation: cost of revenue is the direct energy Con Edison buys and passes through to customers — purchased power ($1,040M), fuel ($42M) and gas purchased for resale ($114M). These pass-through costs are recovered from customers and do not by themselves change profit. Other income is shown net of interest expense, following the 10-Q statement layout.
follow100Note: Rows are rounded to the nearest cent per $100; the chain adds to $15.60 of profit per $100 versus the $15.59 shown, a 1-cent rounding difference.

takeaways.title: Rates, not volume, drive growth
takeaways.text: Electric revenue rose 9% to $4,395M. Under New York's rate plans, Con Edison earns on its rate base — the regulated value of grid assets — so approved rate increases for grid investment, not extra electricity use, did most of the work. Gas revenue rose 5% to $455M.

takeaways.title: Profit rose 11%
takeaways.text: Net income rose from $688M to $766M and diluted EPS from $1.90 to $2.06. Operating income rose 21% to $1,170M as operations and maintenance costs actually fell 2%, more than offsetting a 7% rise in property and other non-income taxes to $1,017M.

takeaways.title: A quarter of revenue is pass-through
takeaways.text: Purchased power, fuel and gas bought for resale cost $1,196M — about $24 of every $100 of revenue. Con Edison recovers these costs from customers dollar for dollar, so they inflate the top line without adding profit; the regulated delivery business underneath is what earns the $766M.
